recent_reviews.author: Paula Serrano
recent_reviews.text: Dear Practice Manager, I am writing to make a formal complaint regarding the conduct of a receptionist during my calls to the surgery on 22/09/2025 at approximately 08:30am. During the call, I provided my son’s date of birth correctly ( date birth ). The receptionist repeatedly insisted that I had given the wrong date, despite me clarifying several times. This interaction became unnecessarily argumentative, and instead of acknowledging my clarification, she accused me of raising my voice, which was not the case. Feeling distressed, I called back and asked for my call to be transferred to another colleague who might better understand the situation. The same receptionist refused to transfer the call, insisting she had already corrected the date, which I found unacceptable and unprofessional. This is not the first time I have experienced rudeness from this particular staff member. As a parent of a young child, I expect to be treated with respect and professionalism when contacting the surgery, especially when the matter concerns my child’s health. I kindly request that this incident be investigated, that appropriate action be taken to address the receptionist’s behaviour, and that I receive a written response regarding the outcome of my complaint. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Sincerely and I will make this formal 100%

recent_reviews.author: Hamaad Farooq
recent_reviews.text: I visited the surgery today while in severe pain and was told my prescription would be sent to the pharmacy. I went to the pharmacy but the prescription had not been sent. I returned after one hour and it was still not there. When I called the surgery, the receptionist told me to wait another hour while they checked with the doctor. When someone is in severe pain and unable to drive, delays like this are extremely frustrating and unacceptable. The doctor was kind and helpful, but the communication and urgency from reception staff needs serious improvement. What is also frustrating is that when staff are rude it seems to be accepted, but when a patient in severe pain becomes frustrated it is quickly labelled as “abuse.” Patients deserve to be treated with understanding and respect, especially when they are in pain and asking for urgent help.
